prerequisites.citation: Victor Kac, Infinite root systems, representations of graphs and invariant theory, Invent. Math. 56 (1980), 57–92
prerequisites.why: The theorem that the number of geometrically indecomposable representations of a quiver of a given dimension vector over F_q is a polynomial in q, and the conjectures on its positivity and its constant term. This paper is the global analogue over a curve, and every one of its theorems and conjectures is patterned on a statement there.

prerequisites.citation: William Crawley-Boevey and Michel Van den Bergh, Absolutely indecomposable representations and Kac–Moody Lie algebras (with an appendix by Hiraku Nakajima), Invent. Math. 155 (2004), 537–559
prerequisites.why: The deformation argument relating absolutely indecomposable representations of a quiver to the points of a smooth quiver variety, by deforming the moment-map fibre along a line of characters. Section 6 of this paper is that argument transported to curves, and the constant C(r,d) comes from the analogue of their characteristic hypothesis.

prerequisites.citation: Olivier Schiffmann and Eric Vasserot, Hall algebras of curves, commuting varieties and Langlands duality, Math. Ann. 353 (2012), 1399–1451
prerequisites.why: The spherical Hall algebra of a smooth projective curve, its structure and its identification with the spherical part of a K-theoretic Hall algebra of the commuting variety; it is half of the generic-form theorem that the whole paper rests on.

prerequisites.citation: Olivier Schiffmann, Spherical Hall algebras of curves and Harder–Narasimhan strata, J. Korean Math. Soc. 48 (2011), no. 5, 953–967
prerequisites.why: The theorem that the characteristic function of every Harder–Narasimhan stratum lies in the spherical Hall algebra, and the construction of its integral form over R_g with the specialisation morphisms; it is the other half of the generic-form theorem, and it is what makes every volume in the paper a function of the Weil numbers alone.

prerequisites.citation: Mikhail Kapranov, Olivier Schiffmann and Eric Vasserot, The Hall algebra of a curve, Selecta Math. 23 (2017), 117–177
prerequisites.why: The structure of the Hall algebra of the category of coherent sheaves on a smooth projective curve — the product, the topological coproduct, Green's theorem and the Hopf pairing — which Section 4 recalls and uses throughout.

prerequisites.citation: Luis Álvarez-Cónsul and Alastair King, A functorial construction of moduli of sheaves, Invent. Math. 168 (2007), 613–666
prerequisites.why: The embedding of a quot scheme of sheaves presented by two line bundles into the representation space of a Kronecker quiver, and the comparison of sheaf stability with King stability through tight subrepresentations. Sections 6.4 to 6.7 are built on it.

prerequisites.citation: Alastair King, Moduli of representations of finite dimensional algebras, Quart. J. Math. Oxford 45 (1994), 515–530
prerequisites.why: Geometric invariant theory for representations of a quiver: the stability condition attached to a character and the numerical criterion in terms of subrepresentations, which is Lemma 6.2 here. The atlas plans no GIT for quiver representations.

prerequisites.citation: Michael Atiyah, On the Krull–Schmidt theorem with applications to sheaves, Bull. Soc. Math. France 84 (1956), 307–317
prerequisites.why: Krull–Schmidt for categories of coherent sheaves, with the local endomorphism rings of indecomposables; Tau Ceti has the theorem for modules, in Azumaya's generality (item 15), and this is the version for sheaves that Section 2 needs.

prerequisites.citation: Günter Harder, Chevalley groups over function fields and automorphic forms, Ann. of Math. 100 (1974), 249–306
prerequisites.why: The rationality of Eisenstein series over a function field: the value of E_{r_s,…,r_1}(z_s,…,z_1) on a coherent sheaf is the expansion of a rational function in the region z_1 ≫ ⋯ ≫ z_s. Every generating series in Sections 4 and 5 is manipulated as a rational function on the strength of it.

prerequisites.citation: Wim Hesselink, Concentration under actions of algebraic groups, Séminaire d'algèbre Paul Dubreil et M.-P. Malliavin (Paris, 1980), Lecture Notes in Math. 867, 55–89
prerequisites.why: The Bialynicki-Birula–Hesselink decomposition of a smooth variety with a contracting G_m-action into affine fibrations over the components of the fixed locus, which is what equates the point counts of the fibres of the deformation in Section 6.9.

prerequisites.citation: Tamás Hausel and Fernando Rodriguez-Villegas, Mixed Hodge polynomials of character varieties, Invent. Math. 174 (2008), 555–624
prerequisites.why: The conjectural formula for the mixed Hodge polynomial of the genus-g character variety for GL_r, to which Theorem 2 bears a strong similarity and from which it differs by the factors H_λ(z); the comparison is the main evidence discussed in the introduction.

prerequisites.citation: Tamás Hausel, Kac's conjecture from Nakajima quiver varieties, Invent. Math. 181 (2010), 21–37
prerequisites.why: The proof of Kac's conjecture that the constant term of the Kac polynomial of a quiver is the multiplicity of the corresponding root in the associated Kac–Moody algebra; Conjecture 8.3 is its curve analogue, and the paper's spherical Hall Lie algebra is the proposed substitute for the Kac–Moody algebra.

prerequisites.citation: Jiuzhao Hua, Counting indecomposable representations of quivers over finite fields, J. Algebra 226 (2000), 1011–1033
prerequisites.why: The generating-series formula for the Kac polynomials of a quiver, which the formula for the constant terms A_{g,r,d}(0) in Corollary 1.10 differs from only by an extra term −l(λ); it is the combinatorial model for the whole computation.

prerequisites.citation: Anton Mellit, Poincaré polynomials of moduli spaces of Higgs bundles and character varieties (no punctures), Invent. Math. 221 (2020), 301–327
prerequisites.why: Theorem 1.1 (arXiv:1707.04214v1, p. 2): for g ≥ 1 and every d, A_{g,r,d} = H_{g,r}(q, 1, α_1, …, α_g), a Laurent polynomial independent of d. It proves the paper's Conjectures 1.3 and 1.4 for g ≥ 1 and removes the localisation K_g from Theorem 1 (items 3 and 8). It does not cover the parabolic and slope-refined counts (items 54 and 55).

routes.title: Counting bundles over function fields: Hall algebras, Kac polynomials and Higgs moduli
routes.brief: Plan the counting of indecomposable vector bundles on a curve over a finite field, the Hall-algebra machinery that computes it, and its identification with the point count of the moduli space of stable Higgs bundles, after Schiffmann. The final theorems are his Theorems 1, 2, 3 and 4. Theorem 1: for each genus g and each (r,d) ∈ N × Z there is a unique element A_{g,r,d} of K_g, the localization of Q[T_g]^{W_g} at the multiplicative set generated by the q^l − 1, such that the number A_{r,d}(X) of geometrically indecomposable vector bundles of rank r and degree d on X equals A_{g,r,d}(σ_X) for every smooth projective geometrically connected curve X of genus g over a finite field, where σ_X ∈ T_g/W_g is the class of the Weil numbers of X. Theorem 2 makes it effective: with J_λ(z) = ∏_{s∈λ} ζ*_X(q^{−1−l(s)}z^{a(s)}) and H_λ(z) an iterated residue of an explicit symmetrising kernel L(z_n,…,z_1), the rational functions A_{g,r}(z) defined by Σ_{r≥1} A_{g,r}(z)T^r = (q−1)Log(Σ_λ q^{(g−1)⟨λ,λ⟩}J_λ(z)H_λ(z)T^{|λ|}) satisfy A_{g,r,d} = −Σ_{ξ∈μ_r} ξ^{−d} Res_{z=ξ}(A_{g,r}(z)dz/z). Theorem 3: for (r,d) coprime there is an explicit constant C(r,d) such that, whenever char(F_q) > C(r,d), |Higgs^st_{r,d}(X)(F_q)| = q^{1+(g−1)r²}·A_{r,d}(X). Theorem 4 is the same polynomiality for quasi-parabolic bundles along a fixed divisor. The roadmap must cover, in this order. (1) The arithmetic frame: the Weil numbers of a curve, the torus T_g with its W_g-action, the invariant ring R_g = Q[T_g]^{W_g} and its localization K_g, the class σ_X ∈ T_g/W_g, and the Zariski density of the set of such classes as X runs over all curves of genus g in a fixed residue characteristic — the density is what gives uniqueness in Theorem 1 and is imported from the LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles Part II (route 3: Katz–Sarnak's curve-family monodromy with DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8:equidistribution). T_g is the maximal torus of GSp_{2g} and W_g its Weyl group, so R_g is the rationalised full character ring Q ⊗ R(GSp_{2g}): identify it with the GSp_{2g} character ring that ClassicalGroupsPartII plans (PAPER-YU-23 route 13, item 099) rather than prove that identification twice. Yu's R_g is a smaller ring, the integral subring generated by the constituents of tensor powers of the standard representation. (2) The categorical frame: classes and the Euler form ⟨(r,d),(r′,d′)⟩ = (1−g)rr′ + (rd′ − r′d) of a curve, slopes, semistable sheaves, Harder–Narasimhan filtrations and the categories C_ν, C_{α_1,…,α_t}, C_{≥ν} and C_{≤ν}, with their finiteness and base-change properties; Krull–Schmidt for coherent sheaves (Atiyah's theorem), planned only as the transfer to Coh(X) of the Tau Ceti module theorems named below, and the computation of the radical of the endomorphism algebra of a decomposition, on Mathlib's nilpotent Jacobson radical and semisimple quotient of an Artinian ring and the ratio |End^nil(M)|/|Aut(M)| = ∏_i |k_{M_i}|^{n_i(n_i−1)}/|GL(n_i,k_{M_i})|; and geometric indecomposability: the Galois descent of indecomposables with its counts (2.4)–(2.5) (published Lemma 2.6), using Lang's theorem, which route 6 requests from ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3, and Springer's neutrality of H² for connected groups over a finite field; for coprime (r,d), that indecomposable bundles are absolutely indecomposable with End/rad = k; and that A_{r,d}(X) depends only on d mod r, by tensoring with a line bundle of degree one, which exists by F. K. Schmidt's theorem (request it from FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.1). (3) The orbifold of pairs: the groupoids Nil_α(X) of pairs (F,θ) with θ a nilpotent endomorphism, their volumes, the finiteness of Nil^{≥0}_α(X), the plethystic identity Σ_α vol(Nil^{≥0}_α(X))z^α = Exp(Σ_α A^{≥0}_α(X)z^α/(q−1)), and the vanishing of the difference between A^{≥0}_{r,d} and A_{r,d} when d > (g−1)r(r−1). (4) The Jordan stratification: the Jordan type of a nilpotent pair, the stratification of Nil_α, the groupoids of filtered sheaves, the three functors π, π′, π″ and the volumes of their fibres, giving vol(Nil^{≥0}_{α̲}) = q^{d′(α̲)}vol(C̃oh^{≥0}_{α̲}). (5) The Hall algebra of a curve: the convolution product and coproduct on functions on the groupoids of coherent sheaves, the extended algebra with its group-algebra factor, Green's theorem, the Hopf pairing on the finitely supported part; the characteristic functions and their volumes, including Siegel's formula for vol(Bun_{r,d}) and the volume of the stack of torsion sheaves, both of which are routed separately as sources of GlobalShtukas; Eisenstein series E_r(z), E^vec_r(z) with Harder's rationality, the Hecke commutation relation, the coproduct formula, the residue presentation of E^vec_r, the truncated series and the Harder–Narasimhan relations among them; and the spherical subalgebra with its generic form over R_g, quoted from Schiffmann–Vasserot and Schiffmann, which is what makes every volume a function of σ_X alone. (6) The computation: the generating series G^{≥0} and A^*, the separation of the torsion factor, the untruncated series, the shuffle formulas for the rank-one truncated series, the residue formula for arbitrary ranks (5.14)–(5.15), the Jordan-type sum Ξ_r̲(z) (5.16)–(5.18) with the bijection between generic Jordan types and partitions, the plethystic identity turning the answer into a product over the boxes of a Young diagram, the generating identity (5.19)–(5.21) with the torsion count A^{≥0}_{0,d}(X ⊗ F_{q^l}) = |X(F_{q^l})| for d > 0, and the periodicity step (5.22) that extracts the residues — and hence Theorem 2, with the rank-two formula as its acceptance test (0 at g = 0, |E(F_q)| at g = 1), and the companion formula for the constant terms A_{g,r,d}(0). Equation numbers are those of the published version. (7) The Higgs side: Higgs sheaves and bundles with the canonical twist Ω_X, their slope (semi)stability, the moduli stack and, for coprime (r,d), the stable locus Higgs^st_{r,d}(X), a G_m-gerbe over the smooth connected scheme Higgs^st_{r,d} (published p. 337), the properness of the Hitchin map on Higgs^st_{r,d} and the stable global nilpotent cone (item 9). This roadmap is their one owner: PAPER-YU-23/036 imports them, and the SL_n moduli space of PAPER-GROECHENIG-WYSS-ZIEGLER-20/62 is a related target, not the same one; the two-line-bundle quot presentation of Álvarez-Cónsul and King with its embedding into the representation space of a Kronecker quiver, King's stability criterion for the doubled quiver, the moment map, the criterion for indecomposability in terms of the line kλ, the smooth family Y → A^1 with Y_0 ≅ Higgs^st_{r,d}(X), the contracting G_m-action and the Bialynicki-Birula–Hesselink decomposition, and the resulting equality of point counts that proves Theorem 3; then the purity and signed Poincaré-polynomial corollaries over F_q and over C (Σ_n (−1)^n dim H^n_c t^n, E9), and the corollary on the stable global nilpotent cone with the corrected exponents q^{1+(g−1)r²} and H^{2(1+(g−1)r²)} (E8). (8) The extensions: quasi-parabolic bundles and Theorem 4, with values in K_g, since the argument given does not prove the printed Q[T_g]^{W_g} (E12), and the refinement by Harder–Narasimhan slope, also in K_g (E11). Mellit's theorem (degree independence and integrality: for g ≥ 1 and every d, A_{g,r,d} = H_{g,r}(q, 1, α), a Laurent polynomial, so A_{g,r,d} ∈ Q[T_g]^{W_g}; item 8), planned here with Mellit's paper (Invent. Math. 221 (2020), Theorem 1.1) as its source; the paper's Conjectures 1.3 and 1.4, with its proof for r prime (Appendix C), are the historical form. Then the conjectures, recorded as open and not as theorems: that each Harder–Narasimhan type has its own counting polynomial, the spherical Hall Lie algebra of a curve, and the two conjectures relating A_{g,r,d}(0) to its dimensions and to a Donaldson–Thomas identity. Import, and do not re-plan: the stack Bun_G on a global curve with its level structures, deformation complex, Harder–Narasimhan bounded opens, finite type and adelic description from Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields (GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), stage GS.0, of which this paper is also a source; curves, function fields, adeles and the zeta function with its Euler product over closed points from Global function fields, reciprocity and automorphic foundations (FunctionFieldArithmetic), stages FA.0, FA.1, FA.2 and FA.5, and automorphic forms with constant terms and cuspidal subspaces from FA.6; Weil q-numbers, their weights and the functorial linear algebra of eigenvalues from Deligne weights, purity and the Weil bounds (DeligneWeightsAndPurity), stage DWP.0; the Hilbert and Quot schemes with their representability, projectivity, tangent spaces and Grassmannian embedding from Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry), stage R09.2, and algebraic stacks from R09.4; the Higgs stack for a twisting divisor, the Hitchin base and map and the Picard stack acting on the fibres, for a reductive group over a curve over a finite field, from Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison), stage ET.2b, of which this paper is also a source (route 4). ET.2b's twist is 'a chosen sufficiently positive divisor', and it does not say whether Ω_X qualifies, so the canonical twist, stability, the coprime moduli space and the properness of its Hitchin map are planned here, in (7); plethystic Exp and Log with their Adams operations from QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms, stage QM.0, their one owner through PAPER-YU-23 route 7 and PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24 route 9 (route 5 of this paper); the Euler and Tits forms, dimension vectors and Auslander–Reiten theory from the Tau Ceti roadmap on quiver representations, which is existing work and is never re-planned. From the Tau Ceti library: Krull–Schmidt in Azumaya's form, Fitting's lemma and the existence of indecomposable decompositions (TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_directSum_of_isLocalRing_end, TauCeti.exists_equiv_linearEquiv_of_isLocalRing_end, TauCeti.isLocalRing_end_of_isIndecomposable, TauCeti.exists_indecomposable_decomposition). They are built for modules, and only their transfer to Coh(X) is planned here (item 15). From Mathlib: the nilpotent Jacobson radical and the semisimple quotient of an Artinian ring (IsArtinianRing.isNilpotent_jacobson_bot, IsArtinianRing.isSemisimpleRing_iff_jacobson). Young diagrams, the conjugate partition and partitions are in Mathlib (YoungDiagram, YoungDiagram.transpose, Nat.Partition) and must not be rebuilt. Beyond these, nothing in this roadmap is in the libraries. The roadmap owns, and must plan itself: the counting functions and their polynomiality, the orbifold of pairs and the Jordan stratification, the Hall algebra of a curve with its spherical subalgebra and generic form, the explicit formulas, and the whole deformation argument relating indecomposable bundles to stable Higgs bundles. It is the one owner of the counting polynomial A_{g,r,d} and of Theorems 1, 2 and 3 with their corollaries (items 2, 3, 7, 10, 11 and 12), of Mellit's theorem (item 8), of Krull–Schmidt for Coh(X) (item 15) and of the stable Higgs moduli (item 9). PAPER-YU-23 route 12 (GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglandsCountingPartII) imports them by node id rather than plan its items 027, 036, 037, 046, 131 and 178 again. Yu's item 037 needs the Higgs comparison in the characteristic range it states, and this paper cites Mozgovoy–Schiffmann [MS14] for a proof of Theorem 3 in all characteristics (published p. 300); Yu's item 046 needs Mellit's all-degree theorem, not only this paper. The conjectures of Section 8 are to be stated with their exact hypotheses and recorded as open; Conjecture 1 of Section 1 is Mellit's theorem.
routes.reason: Nothing in the atlas goes in this direction. The subject is the enumeration of indecomposable vector bundles on a curve over a finite field, the Hall algebra of the category of coherent sheaves on that curve with its spherical subalgebra and its generic form, and the comparison of the answer with the point count of the moduli space of stable Higgs bundles. Searches of the layer descriptions return no occurrence of 'Hall algebra', of 'Kac polynomial', of 'character variety', of 'nilpotent cone' in this sense, or of any counting problem for bundles. What the atlas does have are the two ends of the story and neither of its middles: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.0 constructs Bun_G on a global curve with its Harder–Narasimhan bounded opens and adelic description, and EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.2b constructs the Hitchin base and map with the Picard stack acting on its fibres, for a reductive group over a curve over a finite field, as machinery for Ngô's proof of the fundamental lemma. Neither roadmap heads towards counting, and the mathematics between them — Hall algebras, Eisenstein series in Hall-algebra form, the orbifold of nilpotent pairs, the plethystic calculus, the two-line-bundle quot presentation and the deformation of the Higgs moduli space — belongs to neither. It is not a Part II of GS, because GS is organised around shtukas and the Langlands correspondence and this work uses only its first layer; it is not a Part II of ET, because ET is organised around the trace formula and this work uses only its Hitchin geometry. The closest existing direction is the Tau Ceti roadmap on quiver representations, whose Euler form, Krull–Schmidt theorem and Auslander–Reiten theory are the exact local model for Sections 2 and 6 of this paper; but a Tau Ceti roadmap is existing work that is never re-planned, and what this paper does is not an extension of quiver theory but its global analogue over a curve. So a new roadmap, in the function-fields galaxy alongside FunctionFieldArithmetic and GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands, which it imports from. One accepted extraction does go over the same ground. PAPER-YU-23 route 12, the Part II of GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands on counting unramified local systems, routes Yu's uses of this paper: the universal count of indecomposable bundles (Yu 046, through Mellit's theorem), the Higgs count (037), purity and the signed Poincaré polynomial (131), the top-weight term (178), Krull–Schmidt for bundles (027), the stable Higgs moduli (036) and the density of Weil tuples (100). Mellit's theorem (item 8) belongs to the same material. RT-PAPER-SCHIFFMANN-16/3 gives each statement one owner: this roadmap for the counting theorems, Mellit's theorem, Krull–Schmidt and the stable Higgs moduli; QM.0 for plethystic Exp and Log (route 5); and the LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles Part II for the density (route 3). Yu's route 12 imports them.

GS.0 constructs Bun_G on the global curve with its level structures, deformation complex and Harder–Narasimhan bounded opens, proves that the relevant bounded opens are of finite type, accounts for automorphisms and central degree, and gives the adelic description of rational points; its acceptance examples are GL_1 giving the Picard stack and GL_n with unstable bundles showing that Bun_G is not a finite-type proper scheme. Two statements the layer needs and does not plan are proved here. The first is Siegel's formula in the shape (1^vec_{r,d} | 1^vec_{r,d}) = (q^{(g−1)(r²−1)}/(q−1))·|Pic^0(X)|·ζ_X(q^{−2})⋯ζ_X(q^{−r}), the volume of Bun_{r,d} over a finite field, together with the companion formula for the volume of the whole stack of coherent sheaves; this is the Tamagawa-number statement for SL_r in stack-volume form, and it is exactly the quantitative content that GS.0's finite-type statements leave open. The second is the volume of the stack of torsion sheaves, Σ_{l≥0}(1_{0,l} | 1_{0,l})s^l = Exp(|X(F_q)|s/(q−1)) = ∏_{i≥1} ζ_X(q^{−i}s), proved in the paper's Appendix A from the factorisation over closed points, the count |N_n(k)| = |k|^{n(n−1)} of the nilpotent cone and Heine's formula. The route also names the Euler form and Harder–Narasimhan package of Section 2.1, which GS.0 plans and for which this paper is a clean written source in the GL_r case.

routes.brief: Extend the universal-family monodromy direction of Browning–Sawin route 6 (Katz–Sarnak 11.4.9) with the families of curves of Katz–Sarnak Chapter 10, and derive Schiffmann's density of Weil numbers from them. Import LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.0–5, EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.2–4, DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.0 (Weil numbers), DWP.5 (the rank-one twist) and DWP.8:equidistribution, and Tau Ceti RepresentationTheory/LieGroups Layer 6 (maximal tori and the Weyl group). (1) Katz–Sarnak Theorem 10.1.16 (p. 299; setting 10.1.1–10.1.3, p. 293). Let k be a finite field of characteristic p ≠ 2, g ≥ 1, and f ∈ k[X] of degree 2g with 2g distinct roots in k̄. The family Y² = f(X)(X − T) over U = Spec(k[T][1/f(T)]) is proper and smooth, with geometrically connected fibres of genus g. For every ℓ ≠ p, the Zariski closure G_geom of the geometric monodromy of R¹π_!Q̄_ℓ on U is Sp(2g). Decompose the proof as the source does: Lemma 10.1.9 (lisse of rank 2g, pure of weight one, with a symplectic autoduality with values in Q̄_ℓ(−1), so G_geom ⊆ Sp(2g)); 10.1.12 (tame at ∞, by the Euler–Poincaré formula); 10.1.13 (local monodromy at each root of f is trivial or a unipotent pseudoreflection); 10.1.14 (G_geom is connected and generated by unipotent pseudoreflections); 10.1.15 (irreducibility, by the diophantine criterion, using the Weil II bound on H¹_c and the Riemann hypothesis for y² = f(x)); and the Kazhdan–Margulis step of 10.1.16 ([Ka-ESDE, 1.5]). Request the Euler–Poincaré formula from its owner; do not plan it here. (2) Katz–Sarnak Theorem 10.2.2 (p. 301): the characteristic-2 family Y² − Y = X^{2g−1} + T/X over G_{m,F₂} also has G_geom = Sp(2g). Katz and Sarnak only sketch its proof and refer to Sutor's 1992 Princeton thesis, which was not read. Step (3) does not need it (take q odd), so plan it only for a characteristic-2 consumer, and then as a source-closure task. (3) Schiffmann, Proposition 4.8 of arXiv v2 = Proposition 4.7 of Annals 183 (2016), p. 321, proved in Appendix B (v2 pp. 35–36; published pp. 357–358). Fix ℓ and ι : Q̄_ℓ → C. The set W of classes σ_X ∈ T_g/W_g of the Weil numbers of smooth projective geometrically connected curves of genus g over finite fields of characteristic ≠ ℓ is Zariski dense. Follow the published proof. Fix q odd and prime to ℓ, and a square root q^{1/2} ∈ Q̄_ℓ with ι(q^{1/2}) = +√q. Let F = R¹π_!Q̄_ℓ(1/2), where Q̄_ℓ(1/2) is DWP.5's rank-one twist, on which a geometric Frobenius of degree n acts by (q^{1/2})^{−n}; it is not a Tate twist. Then F is ι-pure of weight 0, its arithmetic image lies in Sp(2g) (the pairing of (1) now takes values in Q̄_ℓ), and G_geom = Sp(2g) by (1). These are the hypotheses of the Katz–Sarnak 9.2.6 form of DWP.8:equidistribution. So the classes with eigenvalues (q^{1/2})^{−n}σ_i are equidistributed in the conjugacy classes of USp(2g), hence dense in T/W_g, for the maximal torus T ≅ (S¹)^g. Chenevier's argument (published p. 358) then gives Zariski density of W_q, hence of W: use the map T × R^× → T_g, (z, t) ↦ tz, and the leading coefficient in t of a function vanishing on W_qW_g. Every fibre of the family is a curve of Schiffmann's class X_g, so no moduli space of curves or universal curve over it is needed. This is how the published version replaces v2's open subset M°_g. Do not normalise by v2's ordinary twist (−1): it gives weight 3. Consumer: CountingBundlesAndHallAlgebrasOfCurves, the uniqueness half of Theorem 1. Tests: g = 1, against Weil II 3.5.6–3.5.7 with the measure (2/π) sin²θ dθ (PAPER-DELIGNE-80/E50); a value t that is a root of f, excluded from U; the other choice of ι(q^{1/2}).

routes.reason: ET.2b constructs, for a smooth proper curve over a finite field and a reductive group scheme in the source's good-characteristic range, the stack of G-bundles, Higgs fields twisted by a chosen sufficiently positive divisor, the Hitchin base and map, cameral and spectral covers and the Picard stack acting on the Hitchin fibres, and proves algebraicity and finite-type bounds. The boundedness statement proved here is of that kind and is not planned: there is a pair of line bundles (L_1, L_2) on X such that every semistable Higgs bundle and every indecomposable vector bundle of a fixed class is strongly generated by each of them, every kernel of an epimorphism from L_1 ⊗ V is strongly generated by L_2, and every unstable Higgs sheaf has a destabilizing Higgs subsheaf strongly generated by both. It is the input that makes a quot-scheme presentation of the Higgs stack possible at all, and it is stated for the canonical twist rather than for a sufficiently positive one. Item 9, the definitions of Higgs sheaves and of the stable moduli space, has left this route (RT-PAPER-SCHIFFMANN-16/6). ET.2b's twist is 'a chosen sufficiently positive divisor', and it plans no stability condition, no coarse moduli space and no properness of the Hitchin map on it, so route 1 plans them.

sourceIssues.locator: the sentence before Corollary 1.8, arXiv v2 p. 4. Published version: corrected, proof of Corollary 1.5, p. 352.
sourceIssues.printed: The source derives the next result directly from connectedness of the moduli space $Higgs^{st}_{r,d}(X_{\mathbb{C}})$ and its stated dimension $1+ (g-1)r^2$.
sourceIssues.reason: The corollary it introduces, that A_{g,r,d} is unitary of degree 2(1+(g−1)r²), follows from Corollary 1.7 only if dim_C Higgs^st_{r,d} = 2(1+(g−1)r²). For a connected smooth variety of dimension N, H_c^{2N} is one-dimensional and H_c^n = 0 for n > 2N, so the leading term of t^{2(1+(g−1)r²)}A_{g,r,d}(t, …, t) is t^{2N}; degree 2(1+(g−1)r²) for A needs N = 2(1+(g−1)r²). The published proof of Corollary 1.5 says so, and p. 351 uses ½ dim Higgs^st_{r,d} = 1+(g−1)r².

sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 7.1 and §7.2, arXiv v2 p. 32; published version, Theorem 7.1 and §7.2, pp. 352–353
sourceIssues.printed: there exists a unique polynomial $A_{g,\mathbf{p},\boldsymbol{\alpha}} \in \mathbb{Q}[T_g]^{W_g}$ […] The proof of Theorem 7.1 is completely parallel to that of Theorem 1.1, using the spherical Hall algebra of the category of D-parabolic coherent sheaves over X in place of the spherical Hall algebra of X.
sourceIssues.correction: Only A_{g,p,α} ∈ K_g follows from the argument given. The stronger Q[T_g]^{W_g} needs a separate regularity proof. For N = 0 (no parabolic points) it is Mellit's theorem when g ≥ 1 (Invent. Math. 221 (2020), Theorem 1.1) and Grothendieck's splitting theorem when g = 0; for N ≥ 1 nothing in the paper proves it.
sourceIssues.reason: For N = 0, Theorem 7.1 is Theorem 1.1 with the localisation removed, which the paper itself calls conjectural (published p. 300: 'Conjecturally, A_{g,r,d} belongs to Q[T_g]^{W_g} and there is no need to consider the localization K_g'). The only proof offered is that it is 'completely parallel to that of Theorem 1.1', whose conclusion is in K_g. This is a gap in the justification, not a disproof of the stronger statement.
sourceIssues.known: new; for N = 0 and g ≥ 1 settled by Mellit (Invent. Math. 221 (2020), 301–327, Theorem 1.1)
